plugins.name: lean-pm-skills
plugins.description: Lean, AI-native product management skills for Claude Code — compress the mechanical PM work into hours and days so you focus on decisions, relationships, and problems worth solving.

skills.name: analytics-insights
skills.description: Deep dive into product analytics — investigate a question, surface insights, build a data narrative. Use when you need to go beyond dashboards to understand what's happening.

skills.name: build-vs-buy
skills.description: Evaluate whether to build in-house, buy a vendor solution, or partner. Use when facing a make-or-buy decision for a capability.
headings: Step 3: Model Total Cost of Ownership (1 hour)

skills.name: business-case
skills.description: Build a complete business case for a product investment — strategic rationale, financial model, risk assessment, and recommendation. Use when you need executive approval for a major initiative.
headings: Step 4: Map Risks and Dependencies (20 minutes)

skills.name: competitive-response
skills.description: Assess and respond to a competitor move within 24-48 hours. Use when a competitor launches, changes pricing, or makes a strategic shift.
headings: Step 2: Evaluate Impact on Us (30 minutes)

skills.name: discovery-process
skills.description: Run a compressed 5-day product discovery cycle. Use when validating whether a problem is worth solving before committing engineering resources.
headings: Day 2: Synthesize What You Know (2-3 hours)
Day 4: Map Opportunities and Rank (2-3 hours)

skills.name: epic-definition
skills.description: Define an epic with strategic context, feature breakdown, milestones, and success metrics. Use when scoping a large body of work for planning and tracking.

skills.name: experiment-design
skills.description: Design and run lean experiments — hypothesis, cheapest test, success criteria, decision. Use when you need to validate before you build.
headings: Step 3: Build the Experiment Brief (20 minutes)

skills.name: feature-specification
skills.description: Write a detailed feature spec with requirements, edge cases, and technical constraints. Use when a feature needs formal documentation before engineering begins.

skills.name: feature-sunset
skills.description: Plan and communicate a feature or product end-of-life. Use when deprecating features, sunsetting products, or managing migration off legacy systems.

skills.name: financial-analysis
skills.description: Run ROI, IRR, NPV, payback period, and cost-benefit analysis for product investments. Use when you need to quantify the financial case for building something.

skills.name: go-to-market-planning
skills.description: Build a go-to-market plan for a launch — messaging, channels, enablement, timeline. Use when you're shipping something that needs coordinated market entry.
skills.name_hint: go · to · 市场 · 规划

skills.name: growth-retention-diagnostics
skills.description: Diagnose churn, retention, or growth problems with data. Use when metrics are declining and you need to find the root cause, not just report the numbers.
headings: Step 1: Define the Problem with Data (30 minutes)
Step 5: Build the Retention Case (30 minutes)

skills.name: metrics-review
skills.description: Run a regular metrics review — pull data, spot patterns, translate numbers into narrative. Use for weekly or biweekly product health checks.

skills.name: okr-goal-setting
skills.description: Set OKRs or quarterly goals — define objectives, decompose key results, align with strategy. Use at the start of a planning cycle.

skills.name: post-mortem
skills.description: Run a structured post-mortem after a failure, missed target, or incident. Use when you need to learn from what went wrong without blame.
headings: Step 5: Write the Post-Mortem Document (15 minutes)

skills.name: prd-writing
skills.description: Write a complete PRD from problem statement to builder-ready spec. Use when you need a formal product requirements document for a new initiative.

skills.name: pricing-packaging
skills.description: Design or evaluate pricing and packaging strategy. Use when setting prices for a new tier, adjusting existing pricing, or restructuring packages.
headings: Step 5: Design the Pricing Test (1 hour)

skills.name: product-strategy-vision
skills.description: Craft a product vision, strategic narrative, or north star in a focused session. Use when leadership needs a strategy document or when the team needs direction.
headings: Step 3: Set the North Star Metric (30 minutes)
Step 4: Build the Strategic Narrative (45 minutes)

skills.name: roadmap-planning
skills.description: Translate strategy and OKRs into a sequenced product roadmap. Use when you need to communicate what's next, why, and in what order.

skills.name: sprint-release-planning
skills.description: Plan sprints and releases — break epics into stories, model capacity, flag risks. Use for weekly sprint planning or release scoping.
headings: Step 3: Sequence and Flag Dependencies (15 minutes)

skills.name: stakeholder-alignment
skills.description: Align stakeholders on priorities, scope, or direction when there's disagreement. Use when you need buy-in fast, not just a status update.
headings: Step 2: Build a Decision-Forcing Document (1-2 hours)

skills.name: story-breakdown
skills.description: Decompose a large problem, epic, or initiative into independently shippable slices. Use when work is too big to build in one sprint and you need to find the seams.
headings: Step 4: Define the First Slice (10 minutes)

skills.name: story-writing
skills.description: Write user stories with testable acceptance criteria, edge cases, and splitting guidance. Use when you need developer-ready stories for sprint planning.

skills.name: tech-debt-communication
skills.description: Quantify and communicate tech debt as a business decision. Use when engineering needs investment in infrastructure and you need to make the case to leadership.
headings: Step 3: Frame as a Business Decision (1 hour)

skills.name: user-research-methods
skills.description: Plan and execute user research — interviews, surveys, usability tests. Use when you need primary evidence to inform a product decision.
headings: Step 1: Choose the Right Method (15 minutes)
Step 2: Design the Research Protocol (1-2 hours)
